body:
I did look into this a bit more since it seems to work in one of the cases and not the other one: we basically do the same thing in the analyzer already, however we only store the result type for identifiers that appear in an expression context, so while the analyzer knows the correct type in both cases, it does not store it into the AST for consumption in the failing one.

So doing the same check again in the editor makes sense and is in line with the analyzer. Code LGTM 👍

<sub>As for the compiler thing originally included: my first impression would be that this should be fixed by reordering calls in the editor, so that the class name index is updated before reloading a saved script. Short circuiting this in the compiler might work for the MRP, but there might still be edge cases with dependency scripts not recognizing the name.</sub>
